ops.line: ADR-001 (P0 gate): TS+Vite+React, JSON file with atomic rename, loopback node:http API, fixed 11-package list
ops.body:
ADR-001 (docs/decisions/ADR-001-stack-storage.md), 2026-11-01, Accepted by the Product Owner at the P0 gate.
1. TypeScript strict, one npm package at repo root, ES modules; Vite builds/serves, React renders.
2. Pure domain core in src/domain/ (validation, graph validation, scheduler, readiness): no I/O, no clock, no randomness, no React; the start date is an argument.
3. Persistence = one JSON file data/release.json (git-ignored), {schemaVersion:1, release, workstreams, tasks}, behind src/server/store.ts. Write = release.json.tmp in the same dir, fsync, rename. Every load is validated with the same validator as import; an invalid file is refused with a visible error, never repaired. Single writer, requests serialized.
4. Minimal loopback API on node:http (no framework), bound to 127.0.0.1 only (a test asserts the bind address): GET /api/release, PUT /api/release, POST /api/import, GET /api/export. Vite proxies /api in dev.
5. Tests: Vitest (unit + integration on a temp dir); Playwright Chromium only, one US-08 E2E (edit, reload, persisted).
6. Approved dependencies, exactly: typescript, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, react, react-dom, @types/react, @types/react-dom, @types/node, vitest, @playwright/test, tsx. No router, state lib, CSS framework, ORM, date library (dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings, UTC arithmetic), validation library or server framework without a new ADR or a PO-approved amendment.
Rejected: SQLite (better-sqlite3 native build; node:sqlite unverified on Node 26), localStorage/IndexedDB, Next.js/Remix, Jest.
Review trigger: data > ~1 MB or ~1,000 tasks; a second writer; a dependency outside the list; a lost or partial write. Lander checks: npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run test:e2e.

ops.line: ADR-001 Amendment 1 (P2 gate): E2E webServer starts only Vite; the test starts the API itself so it can kill/restart it
ops.body: ADR-001 Amendment 1 (2026-11-02), accepted by the Product Owner at the P2 gate; appended, the ADR text was not edited. The ADR said that in the E2E test one npm script starts both servers (cited there as decision point 37). In P2 (#22, PR #27) the single command is still `npm run test:e2e`, but Playwright's webServer starts only Vite; the test starts the API as a child process, because it must kill and restart it to prove persistence across an app restart (US-07). Objectives unchanged: edit, reload, restart, data still persisted; run twice with a fresh store; run by the lander. Reviewer #6253/#6329 judged it a reasonable implementation of the intent. Evidence: experiments/P2/LOG.md.

ops.line: ADR-002 (P0 gate) §1-§9: start date, integer estimates, Mon-Fri, id tie-break, driving chain, gates, validation
ops.body:
ADR-002, Accepted by the PO at the P0 gate (2026-11-01). Task: id, stream (FW|SPS|Security|App|QA), status todo|in_progress|done, estimateDays, targetDate?, predecessors, gate?; blocked is derived.
§1 Start = release.startDate (required input, never the clock); weekend start: day 0 = next Monday.
§2 estimateDays integer; fractions/negatives/NaN rejected, never rounded; 1..250 (gates may be 0); not-done = remaining work; done = finished before day 0.
§3 Mon-Fri, no holidays; start s, d days: occupies s..s+d-1, finishes end of day s+d-1; UTC dates.
§4 One task per stream per day, no splitting.
§5 Serial list scheduling: earliest = max(1+max predecessor finish, streamFree); pick smallest earliest, ties by task id ascending; 0-day gate finishes earliest-1, ignores streamFree; capacityBinder = task that last set streamFree; input order irrelevant.
§6 targetDates never constrain; slipDays = forecast vs target (positive = late); release finish = latest finish.
§7 Blocking predecessor = direct non-done predecessor. Blocking task = non-done (direct/transitive) predecessor of a mandatory gate; done with an open predecessor is allowed but an inconsistency. Driving chain: from the open task with latest finish (tie smallest id) step back to a non-done predecessor with finish = s-1 (smallest id), else the capacityBinder with finish = s-1, else stop. Critical blocker = blocking task on that chain (UI: 'driving chain under v1 capacity assumptions').
§8 Gate = task with gate fw-integrated, security-verified, app-integration or qa-complete, each exactly once (duplicate = error; missing = NOT READY 'gate <name> not defined'). READY iff all four exist, are done, and no blocking task; reasons in order: missing gates, open gates, blocking tasks, inconsistencies.
§9 Validate the whole document first; a rejection leaves stored data unchanged. Reject: missing/empty/duplicate id, unknown/self/repeated predecessor, cycle (DFS, ascending id), bad stream/status/date/estimate, duplicate gate.

ops.line: ADR-002 Clarif. 1: slipDays = working days in (target, finish]; weekend target = prior Friday; done finish = day -1
ops.body: ADR-002 Clarification 1 (P1, issue #7; reviewed and accepted by the PO at the P1 gate; adds no new behaviour). Reading of §6 slipDays: when the forecast finish is after the target, slip = +(working days in (target, finish]); when before, slip = -(working days in (finish, target]); equal dates = 0. A weekend target date counts as the Friday before it. A done task's forecast finish is day -1, the working day before day 0. Evidence: experiments/P1/LOG.md (ADR-002 findings), docs/decisions/ADR-002-scheduling-semantics.md.

ops.line: ADR-002 Clarification 2: an inconsistency never makes a release NOT READY alone; listed last among reasons, sorted by id
ops.body: ADR-002 Clarification 2 (P1, issue #8; accepted by the PO at the P1 gate; no new behaviour). Applies §7/§8 literally: an inconsistency (a done task with an open predecessor) never makes the release NOT READY on its own. When the release is NOT READY for another reason, each inconsistency is listed last among the reasons, sorted by task id. Inconsistencies are always exposed in their own list (P2 defect D6: the dashboard hid them when READY). Consequence: once all four gates are done, any remaining blocking task sits upstream of a done gate, so some done task on that path is an inconsistency, and a 'blocking tasks' reason comes with an inconsistency reason (worker #2901, QA #3125). Evidence: experiments/P1/LOG.md.

ops.line: ADR-002 Clarification 3: title, ownerRole, workstreams get structural checks only (string or array of strings, empty ok)
ops.body: ADR-002 Clarification 3 (P1, issue #6; accepted by the PO at the P1 gate; no new behaviour). Fields that §9 does not name (title, ownerRole, workstreams) get structural checks only: they must be a string, or an array of strings for workstreams; empty values are allowed. Evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-002-scheduling-semantics.md, experiments/P1/LOG.md.

ops.line: ADR-002 Clarif. 4: cycle = DFS stack slice from the revisited task; A->B->A = [A,B]; self-link is never also a cycle
ops.body: ADR-002 Clarification 4 (P1, issue #6; accepted by the PO at the P1 gate; no new behaviour). Cycle report: the cycle is the depth-first-search stack slice from the revisited task to the current one, in visiting order along predecessor edges. Example: A->B->A is reported as ["A","B"] with message `dependency cycle: A -> B -> A`. Ascending order means code-unit order, as in §5. A self-link is reported only as a self-link, never also as a cycle. Evidence: docs/decisions/ADR-002-scheduling-semantics.md.

ops.line: ADR-002 Clarif. 5: no cycle search when an id is missing/duplicated or a task is not an object; only those errors
ops.body: ADR-002 Clarification 5 (P1, issue #6; accepted by the PO at the P1 gate; no new behaviour). When an id is missing or duplicated, or a task is not an object, the cycle search is skipped and only those errors are reported. A cycle among valid ids is reported once they are fixed. Origin: P1 defect D3 (a contract gap, not a code defect): blind QA #2069 expected a cycle error alongside duplicate/missing ids on its first pass (205/206); the coordinator's contract skips the search, the QA assertion was adjusted and reviewer #2418 judged that justified. Evidence: experiments/P1/LOG.md.

ops.body:

Evidence experiments/P1/LOG.md: coordinator #1510 (opus-5-5), 2026-11-01 13:47-14:47 UTC. Issues -> PRs: #5 scaffold/lander checks #12, #6 validation #13, #9 fixture #14, #7 scheduler #15, #8 blocking/driving chain/readiness #16. 587 tests in 9 files, typecheck exit 0 at every merge. Blind QA suites 206/135/69 tests (first pass 205/206, 135/135, 69/69). 5 defects: D1 `{toString:0}` threw in error messages (#6), D2 Date.UTC maps years 0000-0099 to 1900s (#7), both real, found by GPT reviewer and missed by Sonnet builder and QA; D3 contract gap (-> clarification 5); D4 README chain note; D5 gate comment. Lander proof PASS 2026-11-01 14:57: throwaway commit 189f889 with expect(1+1).toBe(3); npm ci, typecheck ok, npm test 1 failed/587 passed, rerun failed: 'not landed: check failed twice: npm test'; nothing pushed. ops.line: P2 gate: E2E twice + API restart, import/export, assumptions all PASS; 775 tests; 15 defects pre-merge
ops.body:
P2 gate (docs/ROADMAP.md): 'Browser workflow completed twice, no data loss after app restart; synthetic import/export pass; UI communicates assumptions' (US-01..08 verified; target 4-6 h).
Evidence experiments/P2/LOG.md gate table, all four PASS: (1) `npm run test:e2e` runs the workflow twice on fresh stores: load sample, edit FW-03 5->8, save, reload, kill and restart the API process on the same data dir, reload, Export link download; (2) the value 8 and finish Mon 15 Feb 2027 survive a real API restart; QA SIGKILL between tmp write and rename leaves the old file; (3) tests/web/transfer.api.test.ts: export->import byte-identical, cycle variant refused with store unchanged, CSV/oversize/400/413 checked; (4) dashboard shows 'Estimate, not a commitment', the assumption list (Mon-Fri, no holidays, one task per stream, whole days, remaining work, greedy not optimal), the driving-chain label and inconsistencies (docs/screenshots/p2-dashboard-*.png).
Checks: typecheck 0; 775 vitest tests in 16 files; E2E 2 passed; build 0; fresh clone npm ci+typecheck+test+e2e all 0; E2E mutation (skip PUT) fails both runs. Issues #18-#22 -> PRs #23-#27 (store+API, dashboard, editor, import/export, E2E). 15 defects (7 P1, security D1 cross-site/DNS-rebinding writes), all found by QA or the GPT reviewer before merge, none on main; P1s were mostly React state races and numeric edge cases. ops.line: P4 gate: scorecard 3.35/5 (A 3.375, B 3.325) = selectively reuse; PO accepted 2026-11-03, follow-ups B, E, A, C
ops.body:
P4 gate (docs/ROADMAP.md): 'Compare at least 3 matched tasks in both environments, record effort, interventions, quality, cost proxies, recovery and regression rate; conclude adopt / selectively reuse / defer.' (Scorecard and go/no-go complete; target 3-5 h.)
Evidence experiments/P4/SCORECARD.md (issue #49, cutoff e0f7c1f): EXP-07/08 (3 matched tasks, 34/34 per arm; Pi 7.4 min $1.58 vs Ultimate 16.2 min $2.72), EXP-09, fault injection (3 restarts, 29/29 provider incidents recovered, no lost or duplicate effects, orphaned Vite blocked a landing), CI on (PR #50). Two blind scorers: A Opus coordinator 3.375, B GPT reviewer 3.325, within 0.5 on all 7 dimensions. Reconciled 3.35/5, coverage 100%: developer UX 3.0, persistence/recovery 4.0, orchestration 3.5, context retrieval 2.5, self-improvement 3.5, extensibility 4.0, reliability/quality 3.0. Band 3.0-3.99 = selectively reuse; no severe safety or data-loss defect. Reuse: cross-family reviewer, blind QA for stateful work, lander with real checks, durable execution and worktrees, project skills, search/pi.usage audit. Do not reuse as is: full orchestration on small tasks (3.6x cost), long-lived coordinators, memory as the only context, unattended 429 recovery.
Outcome: PO accepted 2026-11-03: selectively reuse. Follow-ups in order: B network fix (PR #59, host CLI flag), E EXP-10 (#60, done), A memory-gap fix and re-run, C report the orphaned-Vite defect upstream. Not approved: 429 auto-Play. Default flow: one worker + independent cross-family reviewer + lander/CI checks. Confounds: EXP-08 model mismatch, small tasks, n=1, self-grading, list-price proxies, one machine.

ops.line: EXP-00 baseline (addWorkingDays): plain Pi 45 s vs Ultimate worker 110 s, both 10/10 hidden; model-confounded, n=1
ops.body:
EXP-00 (P0 T7; experiments/EXP-00/SUMMARY.md, RUN-20261101-01/02, instrumentation-check.md). Hypothesis (Run B): an Ultimate worker completes the same task first pass with 0 interventions. Task: TypeScript ESM addWorkingDays(start, days) skipping weekends, node --test; same verbatim prompt, 10-case hidden suite written first (run B first, then A). Outcome PASS for both.
Numbers: A plain Pi (anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 medium, empty dir): 45 s, 54,524 tokens, $0.167, 3 turns/2 tool calls, own tests 20/20. B Ultimate worker (github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5 xhigh, repo worktree, commit 95549e6): 110 s, 392,108 tokens, $0.262, 14 model/13 tool calls, own tests 19/19, also committed and wrote an acceptance report. Both 10/10 hidden in 3 time zones, 0 interventions. Plain Pi ~2.4x faster, ~7x fewer tokens.
Finding: the one unspecified case (weekend start, days > 0) diverged: Pi Sat+1 = Tue, Ultimate Sat+1 = Mon (Excel WORKDAY, flagged as a decision) = prompt ambiguity, not a defect.
Confound: CONFOUNDED by model, since the subagent tool has no per-run model override (NOT AVAILABLE); also different start context (empty dir vs AGENTS.md) and n=1 on a tiny task; grader coordinator #197 is part of the system under test; coordinator overhead excluded; USD are list-price proxies.
Instrumentation check (tools/metrics/conversation-metrics.js): PASS, extracts times, calls, tokens, cost from Ultimate APIs; trace keeps newest 1000 rows / 7 days; pi.usage vs trace disagree on summary-model calls.

ops.line: EXP-01 context recovery: early P0 memory-only probe 10/10 (7 memory calls), self-authored; proper run PENDING at P3 gate
ops.body:
EXP-01 (experiments/EXP-01/RUN-20261101-01.md; pass condition in docs/EVALUATION.md: no critical decision lost, >=90% of 10 fact questions). Hypothesis: a fresh branch recovers key project facts and decisions from project memory alone, scoring >=9/10. Run 2026-11-01 13:00 UTC by root #52; probe branch #1163 (claude-code opus-5-5); 8 memories in the index (project-purpose, repo-layout-and-state, evidence-rules, p0-decisions, environment-facts, user-quang, user-instructions-1/2). Rules: memory only, no repo files, bash or conversation search, 'NOT IN MEMORY' instead of guessing.
Result: 10/10 correct, 0 NOT IN MEMORY; trace showed 7 `memory` tool calls and no other tools; <1 agent minute (4.5 s traced); tokens opus 51,032 ($0.159 proxy) + sonnet 5,417 (summaries). Outcome: PASS for this narrow probe only.
Main confound: the memory author (root) also wrote the questions and the answer key, so it tests exactly what was stored; it shows retrieval works, not that memory captures what matters unprompted. Tiny memory set, same day, no compaction. Follow-up: EXP-01 proper in P3 with questions written after the work, ideally by the PO. At the P3 gate (experiments/P3/GATE_SUMMARY.md) EXP-01 stood as PENDING (the PO's 10 questions).

ops.line: EXP-02 durability PASS (n=1): host restart mid-worker, resumed in ~28 s, byte-identical files, no duplicate commit
ops.body:
EXP-02 (experiments/EXP-02/RUN-20261102-01.md; issue #32; 2026-11-02 06:50-06:53 UTC). Hypothesis: a safe host restart while a subagent has uncommitted edits resumes the subagent with no lost committed edit and no duplicate effect. Setup: builder #7486 (worker, sonnet-5.5 xhigh) at a01939c with e2e/persist.spec.ts modified and e2e/api.ts untracked, snapshot at 06:50:44Z outside the repo; restart by @ultimate #52 at 06:51:01Z (core generation 1 -> 2, same build 74a1c078628b).
Result: PASS. Resumed: yes; the in-flight bash returned 'Tool bash was interrupted and may have partially run' at 06:51:29, next model call 0.7 s later; ~28 s from restart request to first post-restart record. Uncommitted edits lost: none (shasums unchanged; committed fa11867 byte-identical to snapshot). Duplicate commits/writes: none (reflog only the worker's own fa11867, ae4bfc4, 6c6680a; QA #7509 committed 78fec14 once). The worker redid its own failed macOS `sed -i`, then found and killed a leftover Vite server.
Finding: an orphaned Vite process (port held) after the interrupted Playwright run; the worker cleaned it up itself (the same class later blocked a lander run in P4).
Confounds: n=1; the interrupted command was already failing for an unrelated reason; safe restart, not a crash. 0 human interventions.

ops.line: EXP-04 plan tracking PASS: plan epic survived a restart, agrees with GitHub #32; gap: no per-unit owner on GitHub
ops.body:
EXP-04 (experiments/EXP-04/RUN-20261102-01.md; issue #32, PR #36, 2026-11-02 06:47-07:20 UTC, coordinator #7424). Hypothesis: Ultimate's plan extension can track one issue (epic with tasks build, QA, review, merge) through a host restart and agree with the GitHub issue and PR. The plan API is available (`ultimate.plan` document and `plan` tool). Epic E1 with tasks E1.1 build, E1.2 blind QA, E1.3 review, E1.4 merge+land, each linked to its child conversation (#7486, #7509, #7963) with status and verdict; it survived the EXP-02 restart (06:51Z) unchanged and showed in the coordinator prompt.
Result: PASS. Plan and GitHub agree in substance (PR body mirrors the plan verdicts) but differ in granularity: the issue has the experiment AC, the plan the product AC. GAP: a GitHub-only reader cannot find the owner per unit (no assignees, one shared account), evidence only in the PR body and experiments/, blockers only by absence; an Ultimate user finds all three. After a conversation concludes the plan stays in Ultimate storage but is not exported to the repo (a runtime convenience, not a source of truth). ~33 min, plan upkeep ~8 tool calls, 0 human interventions.
Confound: one coordinator and one issue; the coordinator wrote both plan and PR body (self-consistency); state/ checkpoint not compared. Follow-up: post plan verdicts as a closing issue comment or set assignees.

ops.line: EXP-05 custom surface PASS: read-only poc-status panel built from documented APIs, isolated test, correct after reload
ops.body:
EXP-05 (experiments/EXP-05/RUN-20261102-01.md; issue #31; coordinator #6576; 2026-11-02 ~03:59-06:40 UTC incl. a ~2.5 h claude-code 429 pause, active ~10-15 min). Hypothesis: a project can add a read-only status panel using only documented extension APIs, test it in isolation before adoption, and see it render correctly after a reload. ops.line: EXP-06 self-improvement PARTIAL: rule js-date-low-years recorded, but workers never read memory; no transfer
ops.body:
EXP-06 (experiments/EXP-06/RUN-20261102-01.md; issue #33; coordinator #8562; 2026-11-02 07:20-07:30 UTC). Hypothesis: a correction rule written as project memory after one failure leads the next fresh agent to fix a similar failure at its root cause, and the agent uses or cites the memory. Defect class P1 D2 (Date.UTC maps years 0000-0099 to 1900s). Planted twice (never merged): case 1 calendar.ts toEpochDay (worker #9330, no rule yet), case 2 view.ts formatDate (repeat #9510 with rule `js-date-low-years` in the index; control #9523 told not to use memory). Workers got only the failing vitest output.
Result: all three fixed the root cause in ~0.6 min (6-8 calls, 124k-175k tokens, $0.08-0.09 each), tests unchanged, 775/776 green. Outcome PARTIAL: PASS on the criterion (rule with scope/evidence, repeat success verified, no unapproved self-modification) but effect on behaviour NOT demonstrated: repeat and control indistinguishable (ceiling effect).
Key finding: the rule never reached the workers. Built-in `worker` subagents get no memory index (only coordinator branches receive <project_memory>); they are offered the `memory` tool but made 0 calls in all 3 runs. A correction rule in memory does not influence the agents that write most code unless the coordinator restates it or the agent definition tells workers to consult memory (needs PO approval). Memory write path works (proposed by branch, applied by root with `remember`, visible in ~1 min).
Confounds: n=1 per arm; the failing test nearly names the cause; the control is weak (both arms effectively no memory). Follow-up proposed: non-test-guarded plant, rule restated in the brief, optional worker override.

ops.line: EXP-07/08: all arms 34/34; Pi 2.2x faster/1.7x cheaper (model-confounded); single worker 3.6x cheaper than orchestrated
ops.body:
EXP-08 (A/B delivery, #48) and EXP-07 (single worker vs orchestrated, #47); records experiments/EXP-08/SUMMARY.md, RUN-20261102-01..03, experiments/EXP-07/RUN-20261102-01.md; PRs #55 records, #56 closeout (main b87f8df, CI green); run 2026-11-02 13:17-13:43 UTC by coordinator #13171; base 7385604. Outcome PASS (complete measurements). Hypothesis: none presumed.
Design: 3 matched domain tasks (link add/remove, gate status summary, per-stream summary), hidden suites 12/11/11 written before any arm (34/34 on a reference), order alternated. Pi arm: pi -p opus-5-5 medium + one self-review pass. Ultimate arm: worker builder + blind QA + reviewer (sonnet-5.5 xhigh / gpt-6.1 medium). EXP-07: a single worker (same model) on task 1.
Results: every arm 34/34 hidden on first pass, 0 interventions. Pi 3 tasks: 7.4 min, 50 calls, 1.39M tokens, $1.58. Ultimate: 16.2 min, 98 calls, 4.39M tokens, $2.72 (about 2.2x time, 1.7x cost). Blind QA = 67-74% of Ultimate tokens and found nothing. EXP-07 task 1: single worker 1.9 min, 14 calls, $0.24 vs orchestrated 5.6 min, 29 calls, $0.875: 3.6x cost, 2.9x time, 2.1x calls, same 12/12.
Defect: Ultimate task 3 first commit cb68e59 deduplicated repeated workstream names (FW,SPS,FW gave 2 entries) against AC1; its reviewer caught it (medium), fixed in 328d977; hidden suite and blind QA both missed it (instrument gap); Pi never had it.
Confounds: EXP-08 model mismatch (Pi Opus vs Sonnet workers + GPT reviewer; subagent model override NOT AVAILABLE), only EXP-07 same-model, n=1; tasks too small (1-3 min builds vs 5-20 target); Pi time excludes clone/npm ci; coordinator share excluded (97 calls, 12.8M tokens, $9.36, 93% cache reads, to 13:53:19Z); grader is an Ultimate agent. Infra F20/F22 hit no arm.

ops.line: EXP-10 (#60): same-model A/B, import preview diff; both 22/22; Pi 11.3 min $1.73 vs Ultimate 10.5 min $1.85; same defect
ops.body:
EXP-10 (follow-up E, #60; experiments/EXP-10: TASK.md, RUN-20261103-01.md, grades/; 2026-11-02 23:50Z-11-03 00:21Z; base f70db2e; coordinator #16926). Hypothesis: none presumed. Outcome PASS (complete measurements). Task: import preview diff (domain src/domain/diff.ts + UI + E2E); 22-case domain-only hidden suite (22/22 on reference, 5 mutants caught). Same models in both arms: builder github-copilot sonnet-5.5 xhigh, reviewer openai-codex gpt-6.1 medium. Plain Pi = build, review, fix passes; Ultimate = worker + cross-family reviewer, no blind QA.
Results: both arms 22/22 first pass and final, 0 interventions, typecheck/test/e2e 0. Pi 11.3 min, 62 calls, 4.94M tokens, $1.73; Ultimate 10.5 min excl. setup, 61 calls, 7.05M tokens, $1.85 (+7% cost, +43% tokens). Coordinator share excluded: 49 Opus calls, 5.1M tokens, $4.80.
Defect, identical in both arms: builders showed 'Complete' instead of the finish date and hid delta/slip when all tasks of a side are done (contradicts AC 10; forecast hidden for completed releases); the hidden suite missed it (domain-only). Pi's reviewer rated it medium, Ultimate's blocking (code read only, no tests run); each fixed in one round (Ultimate 45f8770). Cross-tests: domain tests pass across arms (45/45, 27/27); UI tests fail both ways on wording/selector mismatch only. No FAILURES.md row (clean run; 0 relay AggregateError in 49 calls with fix B).
Confounds: n=1; Pi ran first; build ~9 min per arm, below the 20-minute target (3-5x EXP-08 tasks); reviewers not identical (Ultimate's read-only definition); list-price proxies; grader is an Ultimate agent. EXP-08's 1.7x cost / 2.2x time gap did not recur; whether model mismatch or the heavier blind-QA flow caused it is an untested hypothesis. Review lessons: the PR reviewer required full cross-check output (not excerpts) and the causal claim recast as hypothesis; grades reproduced from the committed patches.

ops.line: P4 fault injection: restart mid-landing resumed w/o lost or duplicate effects; orphaned Vite blocked it; 29/29 recovered
ops.body:
P4 fault injection (issue #49; experiments/P4/FAULT_INJECTION.md; coordinator #15503; restarts by @ultimate #52). A: controlled host restart while the lander integrates a docs-only change. Attempt 1 (0ba0b14) missed the window (landed 7 s before the swap). Attempt 2 (64ac4b8): the restart hit the E2E check; the lander resumed the same submission 4.8 s after the new core started (28.8 s after the request), reused the 3 memoized checks (npm ci, typecheck, npm test) and reran only E2E. Lost effects: none; duplicates: none (one fast-forward per tip, one landed event and report each, no extra PRs).
DEFECT (medium, Ultimate): a host restart does not stop the child processes of an in-flight check. The orphaned Vite server (re-parented to pid 1) held the fixed port 5273, the resumed E2E failed twice ('already used'), the landing was refused (failed closed); a manual kill + resubmit was needed; recovery 100.9 s (43 s to find the orphan; ~42 s estimated without). 2 of 2 restarts with an E2E in flight left an orphan (also EXP-02). Verdict: durable lander resume PASS; landing without intervention FAIL.
B: all real provider failures to 2026-11-02 17:16Z: 36 failed calls in 29 incidents (28 relay AggregateError, 5 x 429 on claude-code, 3 other: WebSocket error, Connection error, 408). 29/29 recovered, no duplicate effects. 15 needed no deliberate action; 14 needed a resume: 9 by @ultimate (6 branch first calls the watchdog skips, 3 failed watchdog retries), 5 incidents in 4 windows by the human, every 429 (486.9, 150.9, 95.4, 179.3 min = 15.2 h; auto-Play off by default). Watchdog retry failed again in 5 of 14. Non-429 loss 26.7 min over 24 incidents (median 1.0). F25-F28 added to FAILURES.md; the F22 row is wrong (its retry did succeed).
Limits: n=2 restarts, safe restart not a crash; B observational and clustered in time.

ops.line: Claude Code relay AggregateError: Node 500ms happy-eyeballs + no IPv6; fix B = CLI flag, PARTIAL pending re-count
ops.body:
Root cause (side chat #13404, PR #54; experiments/P4/FAILURES.md): pi-claude-code's turn relay in the host core opens a fresh https connection to api.anthropic.com every turn; this Mac has no IPv6 route (curl -6 exit 7); Node 26.7 happy-eyeballs gives each attempt 500 ms, so when IPv4 takes >500 ms and IPv6 fails at once -> empty AggregateError [ETIMEDOUT v4, EHOSTUNREACH v6]. Probe, 15 fresh connects at default: 14 ok, 1 failed after 526 ms; 100 ms fails on demand; 2000 ms 3/3 ok. Scale: 28 of 36 failed model calls in P0-P4 (FAULT_INJECTION.md).
Fix B (PR #59, f70db2e, experiments/P4/NETWORK_FIX.md): PO chose option A, a CLI flag (narrower than NODE_OPTIONS, option B). Quang relaunched Ultimate at 2026-11-02 23:42:52Z with `node --network-family-autoselection-attempt-timeout=2000 /Users/mun/Projects/ultimate/bin/ultimate.ts`; fork() passes it to the core, spawned tools keep 500 ms. The `restart` tool does NOT apply it (re-forks from the old supervisor); after any manual relaunch without the flag the fix is gone. Rollback: Ctrl+C, then `ultimate`. After: probe under the flag 20/20 ok (network calm, so no gain shown, no harm); 6 relay calls 0 errors; e2e 7 passed.
Baseline: 25/1036 Claude Code calls failed (2.4%) in 2026-11-01 18:15Z..11-02 18:15Z. Re-count due >= 2026-11-03 23:43Z (automation 'Network fix B: 24 h relay re-count'): PASS = 0 errors over >=300 calls; <300 = extend; any = not effective. PARTIAL until then. Other options: disable IPv6; upstream pi-claude-code fix.
